tagline.text: A viewpoint park in inland Bohol that looks over the Chocolate Hills with fewer crowds

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 1–2 hours (as a stop on a tour)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱50–150 (per person, entrance and snacks, excluding transport)

children.text: Sagbayan Peak is a viewpoint park on a high ridge in Sagbayan, inland Bohol, where you can look over the Chocolate Hills in peace. It has a butterfly dome, a tarsier exhibit, and a cafe, and the low entrance fee makes it an easy add-on to a Chocolate Hills tour.

Sagbayan Peak is a viewpoint park in the municipality of Sagbayan in central-northern Bohol. Wikipedia describes it as a tourism site with a viewing facility overlooking a valley and a children's playground, and says it is not within the main Chocolate Hills area but offers views of similar hill formations. It is much less crowded than the well-known Chocolate Hills viewpoint in Carmen, and because the ridge is higher, the mornings are said to be breezy and cool.
Sagbayan is a rural municipality of about 25,000 people with an area of about
70 km²
, at an elevation of about

according to Wikipedia. It was created in 1949 under the name Borja and renamed Sagbayan in 1957, and because it was near the epicenter of the magnitude 7.2 Bohol earthquake in 2013, its town hall was destroyed. Because it is a rural area with few tourism facilities, it helps to know that a park like this provides a few local jobs.
By road, it is about

from Tagbilaran (figures vary by source). It lies along the Trans-Central Highway just beyond the Chocolate Hills in Carmen, so most people visit the Chocolate Hills viewpoint first and continue here. The point travelers most often get wrong is that this is not the Chocolate Hills themselves. Descriptions say the hills appear more scattered and the valley floor is visible, so if you expect a dense field of Chocolate Hills the view will feel a little different. In exchange, it is a good place to take photos and relax in peace. The park has a 360-degree viewing deck, and on clear days guides say you can see the Chocolate Hills to the southeast and east, the Bohol Sea to the north, and Cebu to the northwest. It also has a butterfly dome, a tarsier exhibit, a covered pavilion with tables, an air-conditioned cafe (Cafe Baudillo), and a sculpture park of cartoon characters. Some sources mention a Tyrannosaurus rex model near the entrance, about
6 m
long and
3 m
high (19 feet by 10 feet). Entrance fees are hard to pin down because sources differ. Many recent reviews say about
per person with the butterfly dome about
extra, one blog lists about

, and another guide gives ₱50–100. Opening hours are usually listed as 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, but some information says it is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays, so it is safest to contact the park before you go. Official contact details, including a phone number and email, are listed on bohol.ph.

For context, the Chocolate Hills are a group of more than 1,200 nearly symmetrical limestone mounds, described as formed from uplifted marine coral over about two million years and protected as a National Geological Monument. The view from Sagbayan Peak shows a scattered part of them, so if this is your first time seeing the Chocolate Hills, see the Carmen viewpoint first and enjoy comparing the two. Seeing both lets you view the same landscape from a different distance and height. In the neighboring areas of Carmen and Batuan, new facilities need environmental clearance, and a hilltop resort nearby was recently ordered closed for lacking a permit, so check the latest notices for facilities in this area.
From the viewing deck on the ridge you can take in the Chocolate Hills, the valley, and the sea to the north in one view. In the morning, before mist or haze builds, visibility is said to be best.

blocks.title: A less crowded view of the Chocolate Hills

children.text: Unlike the Carmen viewpoint, tour groups do not crowd in, so you can take in the view slowly. The hills look more scattered, but you can see all the way down to the valley floor.
A small dome where you can see butterflies that live in Bohol up close. Some guides mention a separate entrance fee of about
, and one review says it was closed on the day of the visit.
The park has a facility that protects and displays tarsiers. Tarsiers are nocturnal and are easily stressed by noise, light, and flash, so turn off your flash and watch quietly.
A covered pavilion has tables and a snack counter, and there is also an air-conditioned cafe. It is a pleasant place to rest while taking in the view.
There are sculptures of a Tyrannosaurus rex and cartoon characters, good for photos with children. Wikipedia notes that there is a children's playground.
Some reviews mention a small zipline about
long, but other descriptions say it crosses the valley, so the accounts do not agree. Check locally whether it is running.
The ridge is high, and guides say the morning breeze is cool. It is a good place to rest quietly if you are tired of crowded attractions. There is also room to compose photos at your own pace.

items.title: A half day combined with the Chocolate Hills
items.subtitle: An add-on to an inland tour

children.text: Set out by hired car from Tagbilaran or Panglao.
Stop at the Chocolate Hills viewpoint in Carmen to see the view.
Continue to Sagbayan Peak. Depending on road conditions, it can take 30 minutes or more.
See the viewing deck and butterfly dome, and have lunch at the cafe or pavilion.
Continue toward Danao or Bilar, or head back.
To see inland Bohol in a single day, the usual plan combines the Chocolate Hills, the Tarsier Sanctuary, and the Loboc River, and Sagbayan Peak is about one more stop added to that.

items.title: Inland Bohol in one day
items.subtitle: Views and nature in one trip

children.text: Set out on a car tour from Panglao or Tagbilaran. Have a light breakfast and bring water.
Arrive at Sagbayan Peak first and see the viewing deck before the haze builds. Look around the butterfly dome at this time too.
Return to the Chocolate Hills viewpoint in Carmen and compare the same landscape from a different angle.
Head toward the Loboc River and have lunch.
Stop at the Tarsier Sanctuary or the Bilar man-made forest.
Return to your lodging before sunset.
This reverses the usual order and goes to Sagbayan Peak first. It has the advantage of seeing the quiet place before Carmen gets crowded.
There are domestic flights from Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG) or Tagbilaran. Airlines and schedules change, so confirm when you book.
From Tagbilaran to Sagbayan you travel by road.

items.title: By car from Tagbilaran or Panglao

children.text: From Tagbilaran along the Trans-Central Highway it is about
, listed at
2 to 2.5 hours
by car or van.
If you book an inland Bohol day tour through an operator or your Panglao lodging, they may include Sagbayan Peak in the itinerary.
If you go by car, leaving early in the morning avoids the midday heat and gives you better visibility. Look up "Sagbayan Peak" in a map app to check the location in advance.
Guides say there is no direct public transport from Tagbilaran to Sagbayan. The closest public option is to go to Carmen and then take a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal).
Habal-habal fares depend on the distance and bargaining, so agree on the fare before you ride.
For a clear view, the
December–May
dry season is the most reliable. Early morning is the best time of day, and in the afternoon haze can blur the distant view.
From
June–November
, rain and clouds often block the view, and after a typhoon the roads can be in poor shape. Check the forecast before you go.

On holidays and weekends the Chocolate Hills area is crowded, but this place is said to be relatively quiet. Still, visitors sometimes arrive all at once, so a weekday morning is best if possible. Some information says it is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays, so choosing Wednesday to Sunday is safer.

The park has a covered pavilion and an air-conditioned cafe where you can have a light meal and rest. Sources differ on lodging: some say there are rooms and others describe it as a day-visit spot. If you plan to stay overnight, contact the park first to confirm.

There are not many restaurants around the park, so it is easier to have lunch in Carmen, where the Chocolate Hills are, or on the Loboc side. Many people use Alona Beach on Panglao Island or Tagbilaran as their base. The Loboc River cruise lunch is well known as a lunch stop on tours, but the travel time is long, so avoid packing too many places into one day. If you leave early in the morning, you can also eat a light breakfast at your Tagbilaran or Panglao lodging before you go.
Go early in the morning for the best visibility and cooler air.
Confirm opening hours and fees by phone or email before you go. Some information says it is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays.
If you see the Chocolate Hills first and continue here, it is on the same road, so the route is easy.
In the tarsier area, avoid flash and loud noise and do not touch them.
Bring cash. Whether cards are accepted has not been confirmed.
Bring a hat, water, and comfortable shoes.
Public transport is inconvenient, so renting a car or adding it to a tour is more realistic.
When leaving Sagbayan, plan your schedule so you are back on the main road before sunset.
Compared with the Chocolate Hills, remember the difference: Carmen is crowded but the hills are dense, while Sagbayan is quiet but the hills are more scattered.
Check menu prices at the restaurant and cafe in the park locally. Bringing water and snacks in advance is convenient.
Entrance fees and opening hours differ by source, so be sure to confirm them through official contacts before you go.
Tarsiers are sensitive to stress, so avoid flash and noise.
Whether attractions such as the zipline are running differs by source, so confirm before using them.
When taking a motorcycle taxi from Carmen, check the helmet and the fare first.
New facilities in the Carmen–Sagbayan area need environmental permits and some have been closed, so check the latest notices.
In the rainy season the roads and the view can be poor.
